cases.name: owned
cases.why: owned-a claims 6 of 10 feed items have a newsroom twin; owned-b says the live run is 2 of 10 AND says so explicitly, under its own heading. A changed number that is owned is the work going well. Rule 5 must PASS.

cases.name: silent
cases.why: THE POSITIVE CONTROL. silent-b is owned-b with the 920-character acknowledgement section deleted and nothing else changed. It still reports 'kept 8, suppressed 2' — eight plus two is ten, of which two had a twin, contradicting owned-a's 6 of 10 — and never says so. One variable removed from a real report, which is the same technique used to validate the drift detector by taking SCHEDULE 13D back out of FORM_TYPES. Rule 5 must FAIL. owned-a deliberately states no IR-feed count. It used to say '15 IR feeds' against the '16 IR feeds' in owned-b AND silent-b, so that unowned change sat in BOTH arms and a gate could fail this case on a difference that does not distinguish it from the owned case. The 2026-08-09 run did exactly that: it failed silent citing the feed count, a reason that would also have failed owned, which it passed. Do not reintroduce a figure here that owned-b restates.

cases.name: reconciled
cases.why: THE NEGATIVE CONTROL. A threshold derived on open-to-close is re-derived on prior-close-to-close and the week's output goes from four names to two, and reconciled-b states and reconciles it. A gate that fires here is a differ, not a gate.

cases.name: uncited
cases.why: A constant asserted with no distribution and no count of what it fires at (rule 1), the 50,000 figure never stating what it was measured over (rule 2), and success claimed from a green workflow rather than from what it produced (rule 3). Rules 1 and 2 co-fire on an underived constant by construction — an unmeasured threshold has no population either.
